body:
Server half of T-364 (the design of record; read it in full first — `git toc show T-364`
from the main checkout, or the copy the orchestrator hands you). Sections 1–5 and 9 are the
contract. Nothing client-side here.

## Deliverables

* `guests` table in `schema.sql` plus a migration in `migrations.py`: `id` PK, `list_id`
  REFERENCES lists, `name`, `locked` INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, `claimed_by` TEXT NULL (no
  FK), `created_at`, `created_by`; index on `list_id`. GC (`gc.py`) deletes them with the list,
  before the list row. `housekeeping.py` gains `guests_list_missing` and
  `guests_on_non_expenses_list`. Account deletion leaves `claimed_by` untouched.
* A `guests.py` module (create, rename, lock, remove, claim, unclaim, serve, name validation
  with the server-message trim/control rules on 1..64 characters, initials from the name via
  `auth.resolve_initials`'s derivation) and the five routes in `routes/lists.py` (or a
  `routes/guests.py`), with the exact codes, check order and `details` of the table in
  section 2. Every change calls `touch_list` so `change_seq` carries it.
* `_list_to_wire` serves `guests` on every list (`[]` on non-ledgers), oldest first then by id,
  with `id, name, initials, locked, claimed_by, created_at`. A pushed list row's `guests` key
  is ignored like `members`.
* Create-time `guest_names` on a list row in `/sync`, exactly as "Guests at list creation":
  honoured only on creation of an `expenses` list, ignored otherwise, at most 50, each
  validated, `422 invalid_guest_name` with `row_id` and `field: "guest_names"`, minted in the
  creation's transaction with strictly increasing `created_at` in array order.
* `_check_expense_against_list`: a participant may be a member, **any** guest of this list
  (claimed or not), or already in the stored entry. Reword the message.
* `closing.is_frozen` per section 4 (unclaimed guest: locked or gone; claimed guest: its
  claimant's status). `check_write_against_freeze` compares per stored key, unchanged.
* `PROTOCOL_VERSION` 3 → 4 in `protocol.py` (the clients' copies are theirs to bump; the
  orchestrator reconciles). Leave `MIN_SERVER_PROTOCOL` where it is.
* `docs/wire-contract.md`: the list object (`guests`), the push row (`guest_names`), the
  endpoints and their errors, the participant rule, the freeze, the error table rows for
  `guest_not_found`, `guest_claimed`, `guest_in_use`, `invalid_guest_name`, and a changelog row
  under "Protocol version". `server/README.md` if it lists modules or tables.

## Tests (`server/tests/test_guests.py` and additions where a rule lives today)

Cover every row of the error table, the check order, `touch_list` on each change, the served
shape and order, `guest_names` on create / ignored on update / ignored on a shopping list /
over 50 / bad name (and that nothing of the row is created on refusal), the participant rule
with claimed and unclaimed guests, the freeze for locked, removed and claimed guests (claimant
voted, claimant left), claim/unclaim refusals (voter, locked guest, not the claimant,
already claimed), `guest_in_use` with a live entry and allowed once that entry is tombstoned,
GC and housekeeping, and the fuzz/LWW suites still green. Each test fails when its rule is
reverted; say in the commit which you checked by mutation.

## Conventions

`cd server && .venv/bin/isort . && .venv/bin/black .` before the suite; run
`.venv/bin/pytest -q` (xdist is set up). Commit on your branch with `(T-nnn)` and the trailer
`Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Never touch gittoc, never push.
title: Ledger guests: server — guests table, endpoints, guest_names on create, participant rule, freeze, protocol 4
